messages:
ben_acme: Hey team — our March invoice (acct acme-inc / acct_98765) has ~1.2M embedding units charged but our dashboard shows ~60k. Can you explain the delta?

maria_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the invoice line and one example request id or a sample request? Also which model and endpoint you used?

ben_acme: Invoice lines: 
- 2026-03-02 embeddings usage: 1,218,432 units 
Dashboard (usage -> embeddings): 61,124 units for same date range.
We mostly call /v1/embeddings with batch requests from our ingestion pipeline (python). Example recent response log: 
```
request_id: r-0a1b2c3d
url: POST /v1/embeddings
body: {"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["doc1","doc2","doc3"]}
response: {"data":[{"embedding":[...1536 floats...]},{"embedding":[...1536...]},{"embedding":[...1536...]}]}
```
No rerank calls AFAIK.

jordan_billing: Thanks @ben_acme — can you confirm whether you also call the rerank endpoint or any pairwise comparisons? Billing for pairwise rerank multiplies embedding accounting (pairs billed) which looks like embeddings but is billed differently.

ben_acme: We do have a legacy rerank job (inactive) but not in that date range. I double-checked logs — only /v1/embeddings from our ingesters.

sam_runtime: Looping in runtime to trace billing attribution. @doug_backend can you pull the metering logs for request_id r-0a1b2c3d and the surrounding batch window 1926500000-1926510000? Also we need invoice trace id if available.

doug_backend: grabbing now. Quick note: we had a batching change last week that collapses concurrent small batches into a single render job and emits an aggregated metering event. If the aggregator failed to attach original request_ids, the invoice/ledger side might attribute the entire aggregated token count to one internal batching key instead of per-customer request attribution. Reproducing locally.

ben_acme: Ah — could that cause counts to blow up? The numbers are ~20x.

doug_backend: Possibly — another route: check whether any of your inputs were truncated server-side. If the embed model is given extremely long inputs and we truncate, our billing code should count tokens after truncation; but an older path accidentally used pre-truncation token counts when emitting the metering event. That would overcount.

maria_support: Can you run one small repro for us? Send a minimal curl that reproduces the path that your pipeline uses (we can replay).

ben_acme: Here's a minimal repro that mirrors our batch client (3 inputs), posted exactly as our pipeline: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-ACME" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["A long document... (repeat 2k chars)","short",""]}' \
  -D - | sed -n '1,60p'
```
Note the last input is an empty string in the real pipeline sometimes (edge-case).

replay-bot: @sam_runtime scheduled replay job replay-1926504321 for request r-0a1b2c3d (flags: --preserve-ids --emit-trace).

sam_runtime: Replay started. Observed path: ingestion client created 1 batch with 3 inputs -> batching-service merged with another in-flight batch (concurrent) -> aggregator emitted metering event with token_count=1,234,567 (pre-truncation) but attribution field was set to internal_batch_42 instead of acct_98765; ledger then rolled up internal_batch_42 to invoice grouping.

ben_acme: That matches the magnitude. Why would attribution be internal_batch_42?

doug_backend: Root cause draft: a race between batching window close and attribution propagation. We maintain a map request_id->account_id. When two batches merge, we create a synthetic batch_id and were supposed to union the account list and emit per-account metering lines. One codepath emitted a single synthetic line with pre-merge token_count and the synthetic id. Ledger then applied an owner mapping later which didn't find account entries and defaulted to a catch-all bucket that maps to the producer (internal) cost center which we then invoice incorrectly to the last seen customer. Edge-case triggered by empty-string inputs (len=0) which caused tokenization to misreport pre-truncation length in that path.

jordan_billing: TL;DR: overcount caused by pre-truncation token counting + batch-merge attribution bug. This produced a mis-attributed invoice line.

maria_support: Apologies to @ben_acme. Proposed remediation: 1) we will credit the invoice for the overcharged amount for March 1-7 immediately (estimate on accuracy pending), 2) deployment will include a fix to ensure attribution is per-account and token counts use post-truncation values, 3) we'll re-run ledger for the affected window and publish corrected invoices. Do you accept a credit now while we reprocess?

ben_acme: Yes please — credit is fine. We need confirmation in writing and a corrected invoice PDF. Also would like an ETA for the ledger reprocess.

doug_backend: Action items: 
- I opened INC-4321 (internal) to track fix and ledger replay.
- Patch branch: fix/batch-attrib-192650, PR #987 (unit tests + e2e replay).
- Immediate mitigation: disable cross-account merging for 24h (hotfix deployed) — reduces throughput but prevents new mis-attributions.
- Ledger replay ETA: run job tomorrow morning UTC, corrected invoices by +48h.

jordan_billing: I'll provision the credit and attach a provisional credit memo to the account now; will follow up with the corrected invoice PDF after replay.

maria_support: Ben — can you confirm the account email for the credit memo and whether there are any regulatory constraints for issuing credits?

ben_acme: billing@acme-inc.com. No special regs. Thank you for quick triage.

sam_runtime: Follow-up: We also noticed a separate path where rerank pairwise jobs (if used) would expand pairs and we've started adding explicit safeguards in metering to emit per-input vs per-pair flags. Not relevant to your case but pushed to QA to avoid future confusion.

ben_acme: Great — appreciate the transparency. Will wait for the credit note and corrected invoice.

maria_support: Closing loop: INC-4321 tracking, PR #987 merged to canary, hotfix active. Next updates posted in this thread when ledger job completes. :handshake:

replay-bot: replay-1926504321 finished: status=success, replayed_requests=4, affected_accounts=[acct_98765], emitted_corrections=1

jordan_billing: Ledger reprocess completed. Corrected invoice PDF uploaded to customer portal and credit memo applied (ref CM-2026-0042). Please confirm receipt @ben_acme.

ben_acme: Received corrected PDF and credit memo. Numbers look good now. Thanks team. :tada:
